title: Mirror
intro: The packet is headed for the mines on the right. Place a barrier to turn it around so it comes back to the target. Whatever tunnels through is probability lost to the mines, so thickness and height both matter; but a barrier that is too short lets the spreading packet slip around the edges.
goal: Place the barrier in the packet's path so it bounces back into the target on the left. Set its thickness, length and strength V, then Observe at the peak.

physics.point: A barrier above the packet's energy reflects it, but a thin one is a leaky mirror: part of the wave tunnels through. Thick, strong and long enough makes a good mirror.

idea: The packet has energy E = k²/2 = 2. A barrier with V well above 2 turns it around. A barrier below 2 lets most of it pass over the top.

Even above that, a thin barrier is not a perfect mirror. Inside it the wave decays exponentially, and whatever is left on the far side tunnels through, toward the mines. For a wave of the packet's mean energy, each extra unit of thickness cuts the leak by a factor of about e<sup>2κ</sup>.

The barrier must also be long enough. When the packet reaches it, its spread across is σ ≈ 2.1, so two σ either side makes it about 8.5 units tall. A shorter barrier lets the edges of the packet slip past.
maths: For V = 3.4 and E = 2, κ ≈ 1.67, the decay length is 0.6 and e<sup>2κ</sup> ≈ 28. At exactly E = 2 this soft-edged barrier transmits 22 % at w = 1, 1 % at w = 2 and 0.04 % at w = 3.
Averaged over the packet's spread of energies, the 3-thick barrier transmits about 0.8 %. Most of that is the few fastest components (k > 2.6) passing over the top, not tunnelling.
The default barrier (w = 1, V = 3) leaks about 36 %, because its soft edges leave a peak of only 2.7.

With w = 3 and length 15, the best P<sub>T</sub> rises with V and then levels off: 28 % at V = 2, 46 % at V = 2.5, and 52–55 % for V from 3 to 6. At V = 3.4, w = 3, a length of 8 gives 33 %, 12 gives 51 % and 15 gives 54 %.
The round trip also costs spreading. With the barrier at x ≈ 25.5 the packet returns to the target at t ≈ 11. At x = 22 the trip is shorter, it returns at t ≈ 8, and P<sub>T</sub> reaches about 62 %.
try: Place the barrier and keep its defaults (w = 1, V = 3, length 8). Much of the packet leaks through or slips past the ends, and the best P<sub>T</sub> is about 25 %.
Make it 3 thick and 15 long, then vary V. At V = 2 about 40 % of the packet goes through; from V ≈ 3 up the mirror is nearly perfect and P<sub>T</sub> levels off near 54 %.
Slide the strong, long barrier left, toward the packet. The packet comes back sooner and narrower: around x = 22, P<sub>T</sub> reaches about 62 % at t ≈ 8.
